sentences.text: Kalwa vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023

Author: Ajay Bhanot
Bench: Ajay Bhanot
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 43877 of 2022
Applicant :- Kalwa

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd Haris Khan,Neeraj Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 404 of 2016 at Police Station- Parikshatgarh, District- Meerut under Sections 395, 397, 412,
420, 482, IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 11.12.2016
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 07.05.2022.

The following arguments made by Mohd. Haris Khan, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Sunil Kumar Srivastava, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
(1).
The applicant was not named in the FIR.
(2). One country made pistol and sharp edged implement has been shown as recovered from the applicant.
(3). The recovered items were planted on the applicant by the police to falsely implicate him in the this case and to burnish their credentials.
(4). The recovered items cannot be linked with the offence.

1
(5). The applicant was nominated in the confessional statement made by a co-accused Shah Alam before the police authorities.
The said statement insofar as it implicates the applicant is inadmissible in evidence.
In fact the car was recovered from the principal offender Shah Alam and not the applicant.
(6). There is no independent witness to the alleged recovery.
(7). Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
(8). Learned AGA points out that the applicant has a number of cases pending against him.

Rejoining the issue and relying on the instructions received by the learned A.G.A., Sri Mohd. Haris Khan, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant contends that the applicant is a financially destitute person.
He does not have an effective pairokar to search out the details of his criminal history.
Hence details of the said cases could not be stated.
But on the basis of records of the AGA and from instructions from the applicant the criminal history has been explained.
It is submitted that the applicant belongs to an economically weaker section of the society and is an easy scapegoat for the police authorities.
The police authorities falsely implicated him in the aforesaid cases burnish their credentials.
The said criminal cases do not have any bearing on the instant case.
(9). The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
The applicant is in jail for more than six years.
The trial is moving at a snail's pace.
The trial shows no signs of an early conclusion.
Inordinate delay in concluding trial had lead to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant and violates the rights of the applicant to speedy trial.

Before parting the Court would like to notice the submission of Sri Mohd. Haris Khan, learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is financially destitute and lacked access to legal aid for almost six years.
Due to non availability of legal aid the applicant could not file the bail application for almost 5-5 1/2 years.

Lastly, it is contended that the denial of legal aid was caused by failure to implement the directions of this Court Directions have already been issued in this regard by this Court in Anil Gaur @ Sonu @
Sonu Tomar Vs. State of U.P (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 16961 of 2022).

entities.text:
Anil Gaur @ Sonu @
Sonu Tomar Vs. State of U.P (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 16961 of 2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid submissions on behalf of the applicant, Secretary, Uttar Pradesh State Legal Services Authority shall look into the matter and see if there was any non compliance of orders passed by this Court in Anil Gaur (supra) in failure to provide legal aid.

entities.text: Uttar Pradesh State Legal Services Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Kalwa vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57861290/
2
Let the applicant- Kalwa be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
